questions.question:
Statement I: A freely suspended bar magnet always aligns itself in the north-south direction.
Statement II: The north pole of a bar magnet points towards the geographic north of the Earth.
Statement III: The north-seeking end of a magnet is attracted to the Earth's magnetic south pole.

Which of the following is correct ?
questions.option_1: Only Statements I and II are correct
questions.option_2: Only Statements II and III are correct
questions.solution: All three statements are correct. A freely suspended magnet aligns with the Earth's magnetic field. The end pointing to the Geographic North is called the North Pole. Interestingly, because opposite poles attract, the North Pole of a magnet is actually attracted to the Magnetic South Pole of the Earth (which is located near the Geographic North Pole).

questions.question: Four resistors of equal resistance R each are connected in various possible ways both in series and/or parallel to get different combined resistances. Which of the following values of resistance cannot be achieved by using all the four resistors?
questions.solution:
With four resistors of resistance R, we can achieve many values, but 2 R is not the result of using all four resistors in a standard symmetric or simple series-parallel mix that utilizes the whole set. For example:

  • 0.25 R: All four in parallel (R/4).
  • 1.33 R: Three in parallel (R/3) connected in series with the fourth (R+R/3=1.33R).
  • To get 2 R using all four, you would need specific bridge or complex combinations, but typically 2 R is achieved using only two resistors in series or two parallel pairs in series.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): An electric iron requires a 5 A fuse to prevent short circuiting.
Reason (R): A fuse rated at 5 A can safely carry the normal operating current of the iron and will blow if the current exceeds this limit, protecting the appliance.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true. A fuse is a safety device. If a fault occurs and the current exceeds 5 A, the fuse wire melts (blows), breaking the circuit and preventing damage or fire from short-circuiting.

questions.question:
Statement I: In the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, the direction of the thumb represents the direction of current in the conductor.
Statement II: The curled fingers around the conductor represent the direction of the magnetic field lines.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_4: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.solution: The Right-Hand Thumb Rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire. Both statements are correct: the thumb points in the direction of the conventional current, and the curled fingers show the circular magnetic field lines.

questions.question: A circular coil having ‘n’ turns produces a field _______ times large as that produced by a single turn
questions.solution: A circular coil with n turns produces a magnetic field n times larger than a single turn. This is because the current in each circular turn has the same direction, and the magnetic fields produced by each individual turn add up vectorially at the center.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In an electrical circuit, if the length of the wire is doubled, the ammeter reading decreases.
Reason (R): Resistance of a wire is directly proportional to its length.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution: Both statements are true. Resistance (R) is given by R=ρLA. If length (L) doubles, resistance doubles. According to Ohm's Law (I=V/R), as resistance increases, the current (ammeter reading) decreases.

questions.question:
Statement I: A rheostat is used to change the resistance in an electric circuit without interrupting the flow of current.
Statement II: An ammeter is used to measure the voltage across two points in a circuit.

Which of the following is correct ?
questions.option_3: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_4: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.solution: Statement I is correct: a rheostat is a variable resistor used to control current. Statement II is incorrect because an ammeter measures current; the instrument used to measure voltage (potential difference) is a voltmeter.

questions.question: Which type of water, due to the absence of dissolved salts and minerals, acts as a poor conductor of electricity?
questions.solution: Distilled water is a poor conductor of electricity because it has been purified to remove dissolved ions (salts and minerals). Since pure water (H2O) does not easily dissociate into ions, it lacks the charge carriers needed for conduction.

questions.question:
Statement I: Iron is classified as a ferromagnetic material due to its strong attraction to magnetic fields.
Statement II: Ferromagnetic materials can be permanently magnetized.
Statement III: Gold and aluminium are examples of ferromagnetic elements.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_1: Only Statements I and II are correct
questions.option_2: Only Statements II and III are correct
questions.solution: Statements I and II are correct. Ferromagnetic materials like iron, cobalt, and nickel show strong magnetic effects. Statement III is incorrect because gold is diamagnetic and aluminium is paramagnetic; neither is ferromagnetic.

questions.question: Which instrument detects electric current by observing the deflection of a needle due to the magnetic force acting on a current-carrying conductor?
questions.solution: A galvanometer is a sensitive instrument used to detect and indicate the presence of small amounts of electric current. It works on the principle that a current-carrying coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a torque.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for determining the value of 1 ampere.
questions.solution: The definition of current is the rate of flow of charge: I=Qt. Therefore, 1 Ampere (A) = 1 Coulomb (C) / 1 second (s).

questions.question: An argon positive ion fired towards east gets deflected towards south by a magnetic field. The direction of magnetic field is :
questions.solution:
Using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule (for moving charges in a magnetic field):

  • Current (positive ion direction) is East (middle finger).
  • Force is South (thumb).
  • The resulting magnetic field (index finger) must point upward.

questions.question: A straight conductor is moving vertically upward in a magnetic field directed towards the north. Based on Fleming’s Right-Hand Rule, what will be the direction of the induced current in the conductor?
questions.solution:
According to Fleming’s Right-Hand Rule:

  • Thumb (motion) = Upward
  • First finger (field) = North
  • Middle finger (induced current) = Towards West

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The neutral point in the magnetic field of a bar magnet is the point where the magnetic field is zero.
Reason (R): At the neutral point, the magnetic field due to the bar magnet cancels out the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution: Both statements are true. A neutral point is a location in space where the magnetic field of the magnet is exactly equal and opposite to the Earth's horizontal magnetic field, resulting in a net magnetic field of zero.

questions.question: Which of the following is the proper number of electrons in 1 A of current ?
questions.solution: One Coulomb of charge contains approximately 6.25×1018 electrons. Since 1 Ampere is 1 Coulomb per second, 1 A represents the flow of 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons per second.

questions.question:
Statement I: Nichrome has a higher resistivity than silver, chromium, and iron.
Statement II: Materials with high resistivity are commonly used as heating elements in electrical appliances.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_4: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Nichrome (an alloy of nickel and chromium) has high resistivity and a high melting point, making it ideal for the heating elements in irons, toasters, and heaters.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is highly effective for making a permanent magnet ?
questions.solution: Steel is highly effective for making permanent magnets because it has high retentivity and coercivity, meaning it retains its magnetism well even after the external magnetic field is removed.

questions.question: When will you find the magnetic field stronger ?
questions.option_3: When the field lines are not seen
questions.solution: The density of magnetic field lines indicates the strength of the field. The magnetic field is strongest where the field lines are crowded (close together), which typically occurs near the poles of the magnet.

questions.question: Which among the following materials allows the flow of electric current through it ?
questions.solution: Silver is an excellent conductor of electricity. Materials like glass, mica, and ebonite are insulators, which do not allow current to flow easily under normal conditions.

questions.question: In 1834, who proposed a law that states that the current induced by a change in flow opposes the effect producing the change ?
questions.solution: Lenz's Law, proposed by Heinrich Friedrich Lenz in 1834, describes the direction of induced EMF and current. It is essentially an expression of the law of conservation of energy applied to electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: Which of the following options is correct for Coulomb's law ?
questions.option_1: Valid for both point and distributed charges
questions.option_4: Valid for neither point charge nor distributed charge
questions.solution: Coulomb's Law is strictly valid for point charges (charges whose spatial size is negligible compared to the distance between them). For distributed charges, the law must be applied using calculus (integration) over the charge distribution.

questions.question: Which law explains that the induced electromotive force (EMF) in a circuit is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through it?
questions.solution: Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction states that the magnitude of the induced EMF is equal to the time rate of change of the magnetic flux through the circuit.

questions.question:
Statement I: Resistance of a wire depends on its length and cross-sectional area.
Statement II: Specific resistance (resistivity) is a material property and is the same for a given material, regardless of its shape or size.
Statement III: Specific resistance depends on the cross-sectional area of the wire.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_1: Only Statements I and II are correct
questions.option_2: Only Statements II and III are correct
questions.solution: Statements I and II are correct. Resistance depends on geometry (length and area). Resistivity (specific resistance) is an intrinsic property of the material itself. Statement III is incorrect because resistivity does not change if you change the area or length of the wire.

questions.question: A light bulb working on a 18V battery draws a current of 3A. What will be the resistance of the bulb?
questions.solution:
Using Ohm's Law (V=IR):

R=VI=183=6Ω

questions.question: In electromagnetic induction, when does a moving coil produce the maximum induced current?
questions.option_1: When its motion is not at right angles to the magnetic field
questions.option_2: When its motion is at right angles to the electricity
questions.option_3: When its motion is at right angles to the electric source
questions.option_4: When its motion is at right angles to the magnetic field
questions.solution: The induced current is maximum when the conductor cuts the magnetic field lines at right angles (90°). At this orientation, the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage is at its highest.
